1 Portfolio definition DEFINITIONCRT-006

Portfolio is an aggregation of cross-margined accounts intended for trading in different base currencies and using collateral of other accounts (in the same portfolio). Accounts included into one portfolio are defined as following:

  • having same clearing code (account code prefix (6 digits))
  • DEFINITIONCRT-414either LIVE OR DEMO accounts (defined by main account live/demo type)
     It's assumed that only LIVE or only DEMO accounts exist in one portfolio → if there is a mix, the system should consider only LIVE accounts

Accounts in one portfolio might have different related User (owner), but it should be a common case.

By default cross-margining is performed based on all accounts included into portfolio. [Next phase] There should be possibility to mark an account to exclude from cross margining, called "segregated account"

1.1 Cash Balances DEFINITIONCRT-1323

As part of migration to new data model (LinkLINKCRT-1328), system should support several cash positions on one account. Assumption: only one balance in each currency can exist on account.

DEFINITIONCRT-1356Status field should be introduced on cash position: Active / Terminated, Active by default.

Currency of the main balance is recorded as account base currency. Change of main balance of update or balance status should update account base currency.

1.2 Portfolio Currency DEFINITIONCRT-927

Portfolio metrics are calculated in the main currency, which is defined by the account base currency of the main account. Account is defined as main during onboarding with specific attribute which can be changed, but expected that it's done before accounts are funded. Such account can be only one in portfolio (should be defined by the last date of main account flag update).

Reserved Cash

DEFINITIONCRT-031

ABS(SUM (MIN(0, OrderCashEffect * CR + order commission & fee)) on all Equity cash flow orders) + ABS (SUM (Non-Equity cash flow order commission & fee)) + ABS ( SUM (MIN (0; Open PL for Non-equity cash flow position * CR ))) + Expiration Reserved Cash

This metric is used to reserve the cash for pending orders and potential losses. The components of this value:

  • ABS(SUM (MIN(0, OrderCashEffect * CR + order commission & fee)) on all Equity cash flow orders) - cash effect from equity and option orders that will decrease account balance (considering commissions)
    Non-equity orders are not considered as the formula already includes potential losses.
  •  ABS (SUM (Non-Equity cash flow order commission & fee)) - cash reserved for commissions and fees for non-equity orders
  • ABS ( SUM (MIN (0; Open PL for Non-equity cash flow position * CR ))) - cash reserved for the losses from opened non-equity positions
  • DEFINITIONCRT-655 Expiration Reserved Cash - according to LinkLINKCRT-771

References:

  • OrderCashEffect is calculated according to the order strategy inLinkLINKCRT-510
  • CR is conversion rate from instrument currency to account currency
  • DEFINITIONCRT-107OCO: Orders shall be validated on the prospective portfolio independently, but only the order with the biggest cash effect should be included in the prospective portfolio

DEFINITIONCRT-069

If Portfolio Maintenance Margin = 0, then Max (0; Available Cash),

otherwise, Max (0; min(Available Cash; round down ((Portfolio Equity - Portfolio Maintenance Margin*100/Withdrawal Level) * CR))), where

  • for non-segregated account: Equity and MM are portfolio metrics
  • for segregated account: Equity and MM are account metrics
  • Withdrawal Level - max Margin Utilization that User can reach by cash withdraw, defined in Liquidation profile (LinkLINKCRT-091). If Withdrawal Level is 0, then it's assumed that Available Balance for Withdrawal = 0.
  • CR is a conversion rate from portfolio currency to account currency by mid point according to LinkLINKCRT-012

Example:

Account 1 (main): Cash 0 USD, Positions: 10 EUR/USD (mid point 1.0772, USD → EUR = 1/1.0772 = 0.92834 (rounded up)), InitialToMaintenanceRatio = 0,5, Withdrawal Level = 60%, EUR/USD multiplier = 100000, Initial Margin Rate for 10 EUR/USD is 0.005

Account 2: Cash 5000 EUR 

MM = Qty*Initial Margin Rate*Multiplier*Price*InitialToMaintenanceRatio  (10*0.005*100000*1.0772)*0.5 = 2 693 USD

Portfolio Equity = 5000 * 1.0772 = 5 386 USD (round to nearest) 

Available Balance for Withdrawal = round down ((5 386 - 2 693/0.6) * 0.92834) = 833.33 EUR

2.1 FIFO Algorithm for PL Calculation DEFINITIONCRT-1739

Average Price, Open PL and Realized PL during cash settlement (for non-equity cash flow) are calculated by FIFO for the instrument types configured accordingly in LinkLINKCRT-1741.

The FIFO algorithm for average position price / PL calculation assumes that each closing trade for the whole history of a position should be matched to the oldest opening trade remaining by that moment.

Example the following position history from the moment the position was flat (zero size):

1) BUY +10 @ 99.00 => position: long 10
2) BUY +10 @ 98.00 => position: long 20
3a) SELL -20 @ 99.50 => position: 0
3b) SELL -10 @ 99.50 => position: short 10
4) SELL -10 @ 98.50 => position: short 20
5a) BUY +10 @ 97.25 => position: short 10
5b) BUY +15 @ 98 => position: long 5
6) BUY +10 @ 99.50 => position: long 15

Please note that for trades matching a trade that inverts the position side, there should be split into two parts (See #3 in the example ):

  • the closing part is what turns position flat (zero size): closing_size = sign(trade_size) * min (|net_size of position before trade|, |trade_size|)
  • the remaining opening part: net_size of position after trade = opening_size = trade_size – closing_size

In addition to that, each closing trade should be split into parts exactly matching opening trades' sizes starting from the oldest available - thus, FIFO (See #5 in the example)

Average Price, Open PL and Realized PL during cash settlement (for non-equity cash flow) are calculated by weighted average for the instrument types configured accordingly in LinkLINKCRT-1741.

The Weighted Average algorithm assumes that PL for each closing trade for the whole history of a position should be calculated based on average position price and not the opening price of the matched opening trades. 

Only opening trades contributes to position average price.

order leg price

DEFINITIONCRT-1291

N/A

For margining purposes all positions simulated from multileg orders should be valued by the price calculated for each leg according to the following algorithm:

  1. Calculate market price of spread, as if order is filled at the current moment:
    spread_market_price = SUM (leg_ratio * leg_market_price * leg_multiplier) / spread_multiplier
  2. Find difference between spread_market_price and order_mark_price:
    adjustment_needed = (order_mark_price - spread_market_price) * spread_multiplier
  3. Calculate total exposure of all legs independently on the sign:
    legs_total_abs = SUM (abs(leg_ratio) * leg_market_price * leg_multiplier) / spread_multiplier 
  4. Calculate for each leg:
    1. Weight of the leg - leg exposure compared to total exposure of the legs:
      leg_unit_weight = (abs(leg_ratio * leg_market_price * leg_multiplier)) / legs_total_abs
    2. Order Leg Price, as leg market price adjusted with difference between order price and order mark price split between legs according to the leg weight:
      order_leg_price = leg_market_price + ((adjustment_needed/(leg_ratio * leg_multiplier) * leg_unit_weight)

where:

  • leg_market_price is mark price of leg instrument (LinkLINKCRT-010)
  • leg_ratio and spread_multiplier are calculated according to LinkLINKCRT-1020, signed
  • order_mark_price is according to LinkLINKCRT-017

If order_leg_price is negative, freeze the price at 0 for this leg and rebalance the remaining adjustment_needed part to the other legs: recalculate order_leg_price of other legs considering that leg with initial negative price has leg_market_price = 0. Rebalance till the moment there is no negative price for any of legs.

3 Prospective Portfolio Definition 

3.1 Modeling of the worst-case portfolio for AF DEFINITIONCRT-016

3.1.1 Modeling of the Non-Equity Cash Flow positions portfolio DEFINITIONCRT-027

DEFINITIONCRT-573For Available Funds calculation, the system should find the worst risky case for non-equity cash flow orders part of the prospective portfolio per instrument using BUY/SELL sets algorithm: LinkLINKCRT-632, that will cause the most negative AFEffectWithOrders (LinkLINKCRT-572). Price is not used in portfolio definition here. Orders are assumed to be executed by the current mark price (LinkLINKCRT-010) and don't give an impact on PL (as fill price = current mark price).

3.1.2 Modeling of Equity positions portfolio DEFINITIONCRT-513

Modeling of the prospective portfolio with the most negative impact on Available Funds is based on equity cash flow positions and orders in ACCEPTED and WORKING states. The algorithm processes orders' combinations as follows:

  1. Orders are organized into clusters, such as 'oco-pair', 'parent-child (ex. if-then, one triggers sequence)'. Individual orders are also clusters of their own. This is required to exclude impossible combinations in the next step.
  2. For each cluster AFEffectWithOrders metric (LinkLINKCRT-572) should be calculated (not considering commissions) in isolation (without considering the current portfolio and other orders). The worst order combination of the cluster should be considered: Ex: for 'if-then-oco' is 'if + worst of OCOs'. 
  3. Clusters are sorted by the worst effect on Available Funds (most negative AFEffectWithOrders).
  4. The first 5 clusters with the worst effect on Available Funds are validated for all possible combinations of orders' execution and non-execution applied to the existing portfolio:
    1. For every selected combination, the received portfolio is dissected into the strategies resulting in the maximum AFEffectWithOrders considering the cash effect of orders' execution (see LinkLINKCRT-511). 
    2.  Available Funds are calculated based on the dissected portfolio according to the LinkLINKCRT-030 (considering commissions)
    3. The combination resulting in the minimum total value of Available Funds should be chosen.
  5. For the remaining orders, not included in combinations in the previous step: if it has a negative AFEffectWithOrders value - it is added into the calculation, otherwise - skipped from the calculation and considered as 'riskless'.

3.2 Option Level 

Prospective option level on underlying is defined by the related to this underlying positions and orders in ACCEPTED and WORKING states. The system should find all possible combinations of orders' execution to get the worst case of portfolio resulting in the highest option level.

The following way of breaking down should be used for each combination of orders' execution/non-execution:

  1. DEFINITIONCRT-516Option positions should be netted by the instrument.

  2. All SELL options must be paired together with another order/position with the same underlying so that they become covered.
    In case there are several SELL options, algorithm should start with the maximum expiration day.
    1. First, an attempt to find underlying that will allow to form Covered strategy should be looked for. If the strategy was formed, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 2.
    2. Then, system should look for BUY option with the same expiration date to form Vertical. If the strategy was formed, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 3.
    3. Finally, system should look for BUY option with the later expiration date to form Calendar or Diagonal. If the strategy was formed, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 3.
  3. If no pairing was done, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 4.
  4. If there are no SELL options, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 1.
  5. If there are no options, then the portfolio on underlying has option level 0.

The highest underlying option level found based on different combinations is considered as Option Level on underlying for validation.

3.3 BUY/SELL sets algorithm DEFINITIONCRT-632

Modeling of the riskiest positions portfolio is used in cases where it's necessary to estimate the risk considering the existing positions and orders, which are not been executed yet. Depending on a specific validation where this modeling is applied, we'd define the riskiest portfolio as one, where the minimum (e.g. for Available Funds) or the maximum (e.g. for exposure limits) of a certain value is reached.

For the MVP version, such modeling is used for non-equity cash flow orders part in a prospective portfolio for the Available Funds metric and for any cash flow orders in Exposure Limit pre-validation. Comment: When we add equity options, the equity orders will have to be included in the same modeling as well, as equity positions will be cross-margined with respective options. 

To perform such a modeling system should find the set of orders in ACCEPTED and WORKING states that have the biggest effect on the calculated metric. To find such a set system should compare the intermediate effect from three different sets:

  1. Current Positions and Buy orders netted across the portfolio (or segregated account)
    1.  Example: Position size is -10, two working BUY orders with a total quantity 40 exist. The affected metric should be calculated based on prospective position quantity = -10 + 40 = 30
  2. Current Positions and Sell orders netted across the portfolio (or segregated account)
    1. Example: Position size is -10, two working SELL orders with a total quantity -20 exist. The affected metric should be calculated based on prospective position quantity = -10 - 20 = -30
  3. Current Positions without orders netted across the portfolio (or segregated account)

The set of orders that gives the biggest effect on the calculated metrics is considered for the final portfolio, which includes all positions and received order sets of all instruments.

OCO: If orders are in opposite directions (Buy/Sell), each shall be included in the respective set independently. If the direction of both orders is the same within the OCO order pair, the largest of the two orders shall be included in the prospective portfolio.

DEFINITIONCRT-557 Multileg Future orders: 

Multileg orders should be considered as separate orders for each leg with the qty and sign according to the Leg quantity * Order quantity. Only legs included in the worst-case set of orders for each instrument should be selected for the final portfolio.

Example:

Existing positions: long 1 FutureA, long 1 FutureB. Working orders: Order1 BUY 1 (1 FutureA; -1 FutureB), Order2 BUY 1 (-1 FutureA; 1 FutureB). 
Set of orders for FutureA: Buy (1 FutureA + Order 1(1 FutureA)); Sell (1 FutureA + Order2(-1 FutureA)); Current portfolio (1 FutureA). The worst case is Buy (1 FutureA + Order 1(1 FutureA))
Set of orders for FutureB: Buy (1 FutureB + Order 2(1 FutureB)); Sell (1 FutureB + Order1(-1 FutureB)); Current portfolio (1 FutureA). The worst case is Buy (1 FutureB + Order 2(1 FutureB))
Prospective portfolio will be 1 FutureA, 1 FutureB, Order1 (1 FutureA), Order2 (1 FutureB)

4.4 Option Level Validation 

At the moment of order place, activation and execution of the Equity Cash Flow order system should validate if the order doesn't violate the Portfolio Option Level (DEFINITIONCRT-515defined as Main Account Option Level for portfolio).

The system should find the Prospective Option Level for the underlying related to the order's instrument according to LinkLINKCRT-516 based on the portfolio positions and orders:

  1.  existing positions and orders in ACCEPTED and WORKING states = Current Option Level on underlying
  2.  existing positions and orders in ACCEPTED and WORKING states + order under validation = Prospective Option Level on underlying

The system should compare received values:

  • In case Portfolio Option Level (Main Account Option Level) ≥ Prospective Option Level on underlying
    The order should be accepted.

  • In case Portfolio Option Level (Main Account Option Level) < Prospective Option Level on underlying, then the system should check if the order doesn't worsen the situation: 

    1. Prospective Option Level on underlying ≤ Current Option Level on underlying
      AND

    2. Order is NOT increasing the quantity of the uncovered positions for the current Option Level. This check is applicable for:

      1. all OPTION orders

      2. DEFINITIONCRT-593orders with closing position effect for STOCK/ETF (as only closure of underlying position may lead to uncovered option)


If both conditions are satisfied, then the order is accepted. Otherwise, the order should be rejected with the rejection reason according to LinkLINKCRT-537

5 Conversion Rates DEFINITIONCRT-012

  • Bid for values with a credit effect / ask for values with a debit effect should be used for conversion of cash legs/transactions.
  • Mid-quote should be used for conversion of all analytical metrics to the account/portfolio currency.

Conversion rates are taken from XT Conversion Rate provider, according pairs received from Corner Bank or converted pairs (see more in  LinkLINKCRT-061)

Example:

  1. The portfolio currency is CHF, and a long position for 100,000 EUR/USD is opened on the account nominated in EUR.
  2. The current quote for EUR/USD is 1.05/1.09. The margin rate is 5%. The margin requirements for the position are calculated as a % of the current market value in the instrument currency, where (bid+ask)/2 is used for position evaluation: 100,000 * (1.05+1.09)/2 * 0.05 = 5350 USD
  3. The conversion rate for USD→EUR is 0.90/0.96, and the margin requirements in the account currency are 5350 USD * 0.93 = 4975.5 EUR (mid-point is taken). Comment: Margin in account currency is not going to be used for portfolio evaluation. Will be used for segregated accounts only.
  4. The conversion rate for USD→CHF is 0.88/0.94, and the margin requirements in the portfolio currency are 5350 USD * 0.91 = 4868.5 CHF (mid-point is taken)
  5. Assuming the same long position was opened by one trade with the price of 1.00 and current market at 1.05 (with a profit): 
  6. Open PL in instrument currency = (1.05 - 1.00) * 100,000 = 5000 USD
  7. Open PL in account currency = 5000 USD * 0.93 = 4650 EUR
  8. If the position is closed, the realized PL shall be converted to the account currency using either Bid (for positive PL) or Ask (for negative PL):
  9. Realized PL in instrument currency = (1.05 - 1.00) * 100,000 = 5000 USD
  10. Realized PL in account currency = 5000 USD * 0.90 = 4500 EUR
  11. Assuming the same long position was opened by one trade with the price of 1.10 and selling by the current market at 1.05 (with a loss): 
  12. Realized PL in instrument currency = (1.05 - 1.10) * 100,000 = -5000 USD
  13. Realized PL in account currency = -5000 USD * 0.96 = -4800 EUR

6 Open PL Breakdown DEFINITIONCRT-1032

Client wants to see not only Open PL, but also % of PL raise or fall comparing to initial cost.

Moreover, when currency of the instrument and account is different, final PL that Client earns or loses consists not only of instrument profit or loss, but also of coversion rate change. It's applicable only for Equity cash flow instruments, for which CR is included in both open and close cost, while for Non-equity cash flow instruments PL is settled only after position closure by the conversion rate at the closure moment.

Thus, the client requires to see % of PL change and breakdown of PL by following metrics:

MetricCalculationDescription
For all instruments:

% PL Gross

DEFINITIONCRT-1051

DEFINITIONCRT-1742According to the configuration LinkLINKCRT-1741:

  • For FIFO-calculated instruments:
    (Open PL / ABS(SUM (open cost * multiplier))) * 100

  • For WeightedAvg-calculated instruments:
    (Open PL / ABS(SUM (average price x qty * multiplier))) * 100

where:

  • open cost is a sum of costs of all opening trades that remain open by FIFO, signed
  • average price is according to LinkLINKCRT-277
  • Open PL is according to LinkLINKCRT-008, signed

Should be rounded to the closest value with 2 decimals.

PL of the instrument itself in % - shows the raise or fall in % of the instrument price comparing to the Avg.price of position

% PL Gross (acc. currency)

DEFINITIONCRT-1053

For non-equity cash flow:

% PL Gross (acc. currency) = % PL Gross 

For equity cash flow:

There should be a fork in calculations based on PL calculation configuration (LinkLINKCRT-1741), but we can assume that only non-equity cash flow instruments could be calculated by weighted average, so formula below is not impacted.

(Open PL (acc currency) / ABS(SUM (open cost * multiplier * CR with markup))) * 100

where:

  • Open PL (acc currency) is according to LinkLINKCRT-1038, signed.
  • CR with markup - conversion rate from instrument to account currency used for the trade, considering conversion rate markup

Value should be the same as Instrument PL (%) for equity cash flow instruments in the currency same as account currency

Should be rounded to the closest value with 2 decimals.

Total PL in % considering cost paid for the position converted to account currency and current cost.

For equity cash flow instruments only, for others N/A:

% PL FX Effect

DEFINITIONCRT-1052

((Current CR with markup - Average CR) / Average CR) * 100

where:

  • Average CR = SUM (open cost * CR with markup)/ SUM (open cost) , where
    • SUM of open cost is a sum of costs of all opening trades, that remain open by FIFO. 
    • CR with markup - conversion rate from instrument to account currency used for the trade, considering conversion rate markup
  • Current CR is Bid for Long position, Ask for Short position, considering conversion rate markup 

Applicable only for equity cash flow instruments in the currency different from account currency.

Should be rounded to the closest value with 2 decimals.

PL of conversion rate in % - shows the raise or fall in % of conversion rate comparing to the Avg.Conversion rate used in opening trades of position

Abs PL FX Effect

DEFINITIONCRT-1109

(Current CR with markup - Average CR)

where:

  • Average CR = SUM (open cost * CR with markup)/ SUM (open cost) , where
    • SUM of open cost is a sum of costs of all opening trades, that remain open by FIFO. 
    • CR with markup - conversion rate from instrument to account currency used for the trade, considering conversion rate markup
  • Current CR is Bid for Long position, Ask for Short position, considering conversion rate markup 

Applicable only for equity cash flow instruments in the currency different from account currency.

Rounded to the closest value with 4 decimals.

Absolute PL value of conversion rate - shows the raise or fall of conversion rate comparing to the Avg.Conversion rate used in opening trades of position

Example: 

Non-equity cash flow instrument:

BUY 200 AAPL.cfd → price 200
BUY 100 AAPL.cfd → price 210

Position 300 AAPL.cfd

Current mark price: Bid = 220/Ask = 222, multiplier = 1, markup = 0.5%

  • % PL Gross = Open PL / SUM (open cost * multiplier) = (220*300 - 200*200 - 210*100)/(200*2+210*100) = 0.0820 = 8.20%
  • % PL Gross (acc. currency) = % PL Gross = 8.20%

Equity cash flow instrument:

BUY 2 AAPL -> cost 200, CR (USD -> CHF) = 0.8, CR with markup = 0.804
BUY 1 AAPL -> cost 210, CR (USD -> CHF) = 0.9, CR with markup = 0.9045

Position: 3 AAPL

Current mark price = 220, Current CR (USD -> CHF) = 0.95 / 0.96, multiplier = 1, markup = 0.5%

  • % PL Gross = Open PL / SUM (open cost * multiplier) = (220*3 - 200*2 - 210)/(200*2+210) = 0.0820 = 8.20%
  • Abs PL FX Effect = (Current CR with markup - Avg.CR) = (0.95*0.995 - 0.8386) = 0.1067
    • Avg. CR = (200*2*0.804 + 210*1*0.9045)/(200*2 + 210*1) = (321.6 + 189.945)/610 = 0.8386
  • % PL FX Effect = (Current CR with markup - Avg.CR)/ Avg.CR = (0.95*0.995 - 0.8386)/0.8386 = 0.1272 = 12.72% 
  • % PL Gross (acc. currency) = Open PL (acc currency) / ABS(SUM (open cost * multiplier * CR)) = (220*0.95*0.995*3 - 200*2*0.804 - 210*0.9045)/(200*2*0.804 - 210*0.9045)  = (623.87 - 321.6 - 189.95)/(320.6 + 189.95) = 112.32/510.545 = 0.2200 = 22.00%

With introduction of several cash balances on account (LinkLINKCRT-1323), new logic of balance selection during cash settlement should be introduced:
